title: Next.js Fundamentals
readme:
FULL-STACK DEVELOPER 2026 - PHASE 03
Next.js Fundamentals

Course lock used in this phase:
- Node.js 24.21.0 LTS
- pnpm 12.4.2
- Next.js 16.3.3 (locked from Phase 00)
- App Router
- TypeScript
- CSS Modules / global CSS

Important: Next.js 16.3.5 is a newer patch as of 2026-09-17, but this course remains on the established Phase 00 lock for reproducibility.

Official references consulted:
- https://nextjs.org/docs/app
- https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/installation
- https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/typescript
- https://nextjs.org/learn/react-foundations/server-and-client-components
- https://www.npmjs.com/package/next
- https://github.com/vercel/next.js/releases

This phase intentionally does NOT add NestJS, Prisma, Supabase, authentication, or TanStack Query.

lessons.title: Create the TaskFlow Next.js App
lessons.body:
Phase 03

Create the TaskFlow Next.js
App
Scaffold apps/web into the existing pnpm monorepo with deliberate
settings, then verify the first browser-rendered application.

Book 1 - Hands-on scaffold

Course baseline: September 17, 2026 - Windows-first - Project-driven - Production-oriented

Create the TaskFlow Next.js Application
We now create apps/web inside the repository from Phase 02. This is our first framework installation, so we move
carefully and verify where every generated file belongs.

Before the command
From the TaskFlow repository root, verify all three things before scaffolding:

Get-Location
node --version
pnpm --version

Expected course baseline: repository path ends in taskflow, Node is 24.21.0, and pnpm is 12.4.2.

Why we do not run create-next-app from a random folder
The pnpm workspace root already declares apps/* as workspace packages. Creating apps/web from the repository
root lets the generated package naturally join the same lockfile and workspace graph. Creating it elsewhere and
copying it later can leave extra lockfiles or Git metadata behind.

Scaffold with explicit choices
From taskflow\, run the create-next-app command using the locked Next.js patch rather than @latest:

pnpm create next-app@16.3.3 apps/web

Choose the course settings when prompted:

Prompt                     Course choice           Reason

TypeScript?                Yes                     Primary language

Linter?                    ESLint                  Conventional, explicit linting

React Compiler?            No initially            Avoid adding a new optimization concept before core rendering is
clear

Tailwind CSS?              No                      CSS Modules first so styling mechanics remain visible

Use src/ directory?        Yes                     Separates source code from configuration files

App Router?                Yes                     Modern Next.js routing model

Customize import alias?    No                      Keep @/* default

Why not --yes?             The current default generator enables Tailwind and other recommended
defaults. For this course we intentionally customize the scaffold so the first
frontend phase teaches CSS Modules and App Router explicitly.

Nested Git check
create-next-app may initialize Git depending on context. Because TaskFlow already has one root repository, verify
there is no second .git directory under apps/web.

Get-ChildItem .■pps\web -Force
Get-ChildItem .■pps\web\.git -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

If a nested .git folder exists, remove only that nested metadata after verifying you are inside taskflow/apps/web. The
root taskflow/.git must remain untouched.

Inspect the generated package

Get-Content .■pps\web\package.json
Get-Content .■pps\web■sconfig.json
Get-ChildItem .■pps\web\src■pp

Notice that apps/web has its own package.json. That is the package boundary Phase 02 prepared us to understand.

Expected scripts
"scripts": {
"dev": "next dev",
"build": "next build",
"start": "next start",
"lint": "eslint"
}

Current Next.js uses Turbopack by default for next dev. The script does not need to mention Turbopack for the
default behavior.

Run only the web package
From the repository root:

pnpm --filter web dev

If the generated package name is not web, inspect apps/web/package.json and filter by the actual package name.
You can also run the script from inside apps/web with pnpm dev.

Verify in the browser
Open http://localhost:3000. Keep the terminal visible. Change src/app/page.tsx, save, and observe Fast Refresh
update the browser. The point is not the starter design; the checkpoint is that repository -> workspace -> package ->
dev server -> browser is now a working chain.

What the first dev command actually connects

taskflow root           workspace       apps/web package            script             next dev

HTTP

localhost:3000

Figure 1 - The browser is the last step in a chain rooted in the monorepo workspace

Clean the starter intentionally
Do not delete everything blindly. Read the generated page, layout, global stylesheet and metadata first. Then
replace starter content with a minimal TaskFlow title and description while preserving a valid root layout.

Checkpoint
•
apps/web exists and is tracked by the root Git repository.
•
No second lockfile exists inside apps/web.

Volume 02 - Frontend + Backend Foundations

•
No nested .git directory remains.
•
pnpm --filter web dev starts the frontend.
•
localhost:3000 renders and refreshes after a source edit.

Volume 02 - Frontend + Backend Foundations

lessons.title: App Router Mental Model
lessons.body:
Phase 03

The App Router Mental Model
Understand route segments, pages, layouts, special files, and the
rendered route tree before building more UI.

Book 2 - Routing concepts

Course baseline: September 17, 2026 - Windows-first - Project-driven - Production-oriented

The App Router Mental Model
The App Router is not a list of magic filenames. It is a file-system model that turns directories into route segments
and special files into pieces of the rendered route tree.

Routes come from folders
src/app/
|-- layout.tsx              -> shared root layout
|-- page.tsx                -> /
|-- projects/
|   `-- page.tsx            -> /projects
`-- settings/
`-- page.tsx            -> /settings

A folder becomes a URL segment when a page exists beneath it. The route is not created by the folder name alone;
page.tsx provides the route UI.

Folders shape the route tree

app root

wraps            route             segment

layout.tsx                       page.tsx -> /                          projects/

route

page.tsx -> /projects

Figure 1 - The filesystem describes both URL segments and layout composition

page.tsx
A page is the UI exposed at a route. In this course, pages should usually compose feature components rather than
contain every visual element and behavior inline.

layout.tsx
A layout wraps child route content and persists across navigation within its segment. The root layout is required and
owns the html/body shell. Nested layouts let areas share navigation or framing without duplicating markup.

Why layouts matter beyond convenience
•
They encode shared UI structure into the route hierarchy.
•
They reduce duplicated navigation and shell markup.
•
They create stable boundaries where state can be preserved across navigation.
•
They make route ownership visible from the filesystem.

Special files we will meet

File                       Purpose in the mental model

page.tsx                   Route UI

layout.tsx                 Persistent shared UI around descendants

loading.tsx                Route-segment pending UI

error.tsx                  Error boundary UI for a segment; requires client behavior

not-found.tsx              Not-found UI

template.tsx               Layout-like wrapper that remounts on navigation; use only when needed

route.ts                   HTTP route handler; not our primary business API in this course

Important boundary           Next.js route handlers exist, but TaskFlow will use NestJS for the authoritative
application API. We will not create duplicate business logic in route.ts just
because the framework can host server code.

Route groups and private folders
Later, parentheses can group routes without adding URL segments, and underscore-prefixed private folders can
organize implementation details without becoming routes. Do not introduce these until the file tree needs them.

Dynamic routes - concept preview
src/app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx

URL: /projects/42
projectId: "42"

The brackets represent a dynamic segment. We will use them later when projects and tasks come from the API.
Phase 03 only needs the mental model.

Rendering tree versus URL
The URL tells you which route segments are active. The rendered tree combines each active layout with the leaf
page. This is why layout placement is an architectural choice, not only a styling decision.

A route renders through nested layout layers

RootLayout

children

Dashboard layout

children

Projects page

Figure 2 - Each active layout contributes persistent structure around the leaf page

Checkpoint questions
•
What makes /projects exist?

Volume 02 - Frontend + Backend Foundations

•
Why is layout.tsx different from a shared Header component?
•
Why might a nested layout be preferable to copying a sidebar into three pages?
•
Why are route handlers intentionally not our main backend in this architecture?

Volume 02 - Frontend + Backend Foundations

lessons.title: Server and Client Components
lessons.body:
Phase 03

Server and Client Components
Learn the server/browser network boundary, choose Client Components
for the right reasons, and avoid turning the entire frontend into a client
island.

Book 3 - Rendering boundary

Course baseline: September 17, 2026 - Windows-first - Project-driven - Production-oriented

Server Components and Client Components
The most important Next.js concept in Phase 03 is not routing. It is understanding that your component tree can
cross a network boundary. Next.js uses Server Components by default in the App Router; Client Components are
opt-in islands for browser capabilities and interaction.

The network boundary inside a React component tree

SERVER Server Components           RSC payload network   compose      BROWSER Client Components

render                                                             hydrate/interact

rendered output                                                              interactive JS

Figure 1 - Server and browser environments have different capabilities; use client marks where browser-side JavaScript is needed

Server Component by default
A component file under the App Router is a Server Component unless a Client Component boundary applies. This
lets static and server-rendered UI avoid sending unnecessary component JavaScript to the browser.

Good Server Component jobs
•
Compose mostly non-interactive UI.
•
Read server-side data later without exposing secrets to the browser.
•
Perform server-only work when appropriate.
•
Keep large dependencies or logic off the client bundle when no browser interaction is required.

What makes a Client Component necessary?
Use a Client Component when the component needs browser-only capabilities or interactive React state/effects.

Need                                     Client?            Reason

Static heading                           No                 No browser state or event needed

Button with onClick                      Yes                Event handler executes in browser

useState/useEffect                       Yes                Client hooks require browser-side React

window/localStorage                      Yes                Browser APIs do not exist on the server

Pure presentational card                 Usually no         Can remain server-rendered

Later API server-state with TanStack     Yes at             Query client lives in browser context
Query                                    provider/query
boundary

The use client directive

"use client";

import { useState } from "react";

export function DemoCounter() {
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);

return (
<button onClick={() => setCount((value) => value + 1)}>
Count: {count}
</button>
);
}

The directive marks a client module boundary. It does not mean every component in the entire application must
become client-rendered.

Keep the boundary small
A common beginner response to a hook error is to put "use client" at the top of the root layout. That makes the error
disappear by widening the client boundary, but it throws away a core architectural advantage. Move only the
interactive portion behind a client boundary.

Prefer a small client island over a client application shell

DashboardLayout Server         compose        Nav Server         interactive island   ThemeToggle Client

children

ProjectsPage Server

Figure 2 - Only the component that needs browser interaction crosses the client boundary

Serialization boundary
Data passed from a Server Component into a Client Component must be serializable across the server/client
boundary. This is another clue that the boundary is architectural, not just a syntax marker.

Do not confuse rendering location with API architecture
Server Components can fetch directly from a data source in some applications. TaskFlow deliberately routes
authoritative business data through NestJS later so business rules live in one backend. The fact that Next.js can
access server resources does not require us to put domain logic there.

Mini exercise
Create an interactive small button or disclosure control as a Client Component and import it into a Server
Component page. Then explain why the page itself did not need use client.

Checkpoint
•
Server Component is the default in the App Router.
•
Client Components are for interaction/browser APIs/client hooks.

Volume 02 - Frontend + Backend Foundations

•
use client creates a boundary; it is not a quality badge.
•
The smallest useful client boundary usually gives the clearest architecture.
•
TaskFlow keeps authoritative business rules in NestJS even though Next.js has server capabilities.

Volume 02 - Frontend + Backend Foundations

lessons.title: Routing Loading and Errors
lessons.body:
Phase 03 Routing, Loading and Error States Build navigation that accounts for shared layout, pending UI, failures, and not-found states instead of only the happy path. Book 4 - Navigation states Course baseline: September 17, 2026 - Windows-first - Project-driven - Production-oriented Routing, Navigation, Loading, Errors and 404s A production frontend is not only successful page rendering. Users navigate, wait, hit missing resources, and encounter failures. The App Router gives these states explicit places in the route tree. Navigation with Link import Link from "next/link"; Projects Use Next.js Link for internal application navigation. It integrates with client-side navigation and prefetching behavior instead of forcing a full browser document request for every route transition. A simple TaskFlow route map / /projects /settings src/app/ |-- page.tsx |-- projects/page.tsx `-- settings/page.tsx Shared navigation belongs in layout structure If Home, Projects, and Settings share the same top navigation, render that navigation from a layout rather than copy it into every page. A component handles reusable markup; a layout controls where that reusable markup participates in routing. loading.tsx - pending UI A loading file provides route-segment fallback UI while content below the segment is waiting. It works with streaming and Suspense semantics. Use it to communicate progress, not to hide slow architecture indefinitely. export default function Loading() { return

Loading projects...

; } error.tsx - recoverable route UI An error boundary lets a route segment show fallback UI when a descendant throws during rendering. Error components need client-side behavior because reset/retry interaction happens in the browser. "use client"; export default function ErrorView({ reset }: { reset: () => void }) { return (

Something went wrong

); } Do not swallow errors An error boundary is presentation for failure, not permission to ignore the root cause. Production logging/observability enters later, but even now the developer should inspect the terminal and browser console. not-found.tsx Use a not-found UI for missing route resources. Later, a project detail page can call notFound() when the API says the project does not exist. This is different from a server crash or validation error. Status thinking Situation Frontend concept Later backend meaning Navigation is waiting loading UI Request/data still pending Unexpected render failure error boundary Potential 5xx or application error Requested resource does not not-found UI Often 404 exist User lacks permission Protected/forbidden UI later 403 after auth User is not authenticated Login/session flow later 401 after auth Dynamic route preview src/app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx This will eventually display one project based on route params. We postpone the full implementation until Phase 06+ when a backend exists. The course avoids fake architecture solely to demonstrate syntax. Navigation has explicit success, pending and failure states User clicks Link navigate App Router while waiting loading UI success failure next page error / 404 Figure 1 - Professional UX models non-happy paths instead of adding them after launch Checkpoint • Internal navigation uses Link rather than raw full-page navigation by default. • Layouts own shared route shell. • loading.tsx models pending UI, error.tsx models rendering failure, and not-found.tsx models missing resources. • You can explain why missing data and unexpected failure are not the same state. Volume 02 - Frontend + Backend Foundations

lessons.title: Styling Assets and Accessibility
lessons.body:
Phase 03

Styling, Assets and
Accessibility
Use CSS Modules and global CSS with clear ownership, then build an
accessible application shell with semantic HTML and useful metadata.

Book 5 - UI foundations

Course baseline: September 17, 2026 - Windows-first - Project-driven - Production-oriented

Styling, Assets, Metadata and Accessibility
TaskFlow needs enough design to feel like an application, but Phase 03 avoids turning into a CSS framework
course. We use global CSS for global rules and CSS Modules for component-scoped styles.

Global CSS has a global responsibility
Use src/app/globals.css for document-wide rules such as box sizing, base body typography, background, and CSS
variables. Avoid placing page-specific selectors there merely because it is convenient.

CSS Modules for local ownership
/* project-card.module.css */
.card {
border: 1px solid var(--border);
border-radius: 12px;
padding: 1rem;
}

/* project-card.tsx */
import styles from "./project-card.module.css";

export function ProjectCard() {
return <article className={styles.card}>...</article>;
}

The filename communicates that the CSS is scoped to the component/module rather than intended as a site-wide
API.

A styling ownership rule
Question                                      Preferred home

Does every page need it?                      globals.css or shared design token

Does one component own it?                    Component CSS Module

Is it an inline state-dependent value?        Occasional style prop, used deliberately

Is it a future design-system primitive?       Earn a shared component/package when repeated patterns justify it

Public assets
Files in public/ are served from the site root. public/logo.svg is addressed as /logo.svg. Keep public for static assets,
not application source code.

Images
Next.js provides Image for image optimization and layout behavior. In this early shell, learn the API but do not add
images unless they communicate product context. Decorative images are not a requirement for good UI.

Metadata
export const metadata = {
title: "TaskFlow",
description: "Project and task management for focused teams",
};

Metadata belongs with the route/layout structure because it describes the document the framework is producing.
Later phases can refine per-route metadata.

Semantic HTML first

UI intent                                  Prefer

Primary site navigation                    nav

Page content                               main

Independent card/content item              article when semantically appropriate

Action                                     button

Navigation                                 a / Link

Section heading                            Correct heading level rather than styled div

Accessibility is architecture, not polish
•
Use real buttons for actions so keyboard behavior exists automatically.
•
Use visible focus states rather than removing outlines.
•
Provide labels for controls and meaningful alt text for informative images.
•
Keep heading hierarchy meaningful.
•
Use aria-live sparingly for important asynchronous status updates.
•
Test keyboard navigation while the interface is still small.

Responsive shell without a CSS framework
Use modern CSS layout primitives directly. The goal is to understand the browser before adding another vocabulary.
The TaskFlow shell can use a responsive grid or flex layout, sensible max width, and media queries where
necessary.

Design target
TaskFlow
--------------------------------------------------
Home       Projects       Settings

Your work
Organize projects and keep tasks moving.

[ Active Projects ]         [ Tasks Due ]     [ Completed ]

Recent projects
[ Website refresh ]
[ Inventory rollout ]

The interface should feel intentional but remain small enough that routing and rendering concepts are visible.

Checkpoint
•
Global styles stay global.
•
Component styles are locally owned through CSS Modules.
•
Public assets are addressed from /.
•
Semantic elements are chosen by meaning rather than appearance.
•
Keyboard and focus behavior are checked before the phase is complete.

Volume 02 - Frontend + Backend Foundations

lessons.title: Environment DevTools and Debugging
lessons.body:
Phase 03

Environment, DevTools and
Debugging
Learn frontend environment-variable boundaries, browser/terminal
evidence, and a systematic Next.js debugging loop.

Book 6 - Diagnostics

Course baseline: September 17, 2026 - Windows-first - Project-driven - Production-oriented

Environment Variables, DevTools and Next.js
Debugging
Frontend bugs often sit at a boundary: server versus browser, build time versus runtime, route versus component, or
workspace root versus package directory. Phase 03 teaches how to locate the failing layer before editing code.

Environment variable boundary
By default, environment variables are server-only. A variable exposed to browser JavaScript requires the
NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix. That prefix is a publication decision, not a naming style.

Example                                   Browser-visible?             Use

API_INTERNAL_SECRET                       No                           Never place secrets in frontend browser code

DATABASE_URL                              No                           Later belongs to API/backend environment, not
apps/web

NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL                       Yes                          Later tells browser where public API is

NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME                      Yes                          Harmless public configuration if needed

Security rule                  If a value must remain secret, it must never depend on NEXT_PUBLIC_
protection. Anything delivered to browser JavaScript is inspectable by the user.

Where errors appear
Symptom                                          First place to look

Build/type error                                 Terminal running next dev/build

Client runtime error                             Browser console and Next error overlay

Failed network request later                     Browser Network tab

Server Component exception                       Terminal plus rendered error boundary

Wrong route/404                                  Route tree and browser URL

CSS not applied                                  DOM class name, imported module, browser styles panel

A layered debugging loop
1. Reproduce the failure.
2. Identify the environment: terminal/server or browser/client.
3. Read the first useful error, not only the last stack frame.
4. Confirm the current route and file path.
5. Reduce the failing component or change.
6. Make the smallest correction.
7. Re-run the same verification.
8. Run lint/type/build before declaring victory.

Common error: hook in Server Component
Symptom: useState/useEffect or event-handler related error in a Server Component. Diagnosis: the component
needs browser interactivity. Correction: move only the interactive portion into a Client Component; do not
automatically convert the root layout.

Common error: module not found
Check the import alias, file casing, relative path, and whether the dependency belongs to apps/web. On Windows,
case mistakes may remain hidden locally and fail on a case-sensitive production filesystem.

Common error: command ran in wrong place
Get-Location
Get-Content .\package.json
pnpm --filter web dev

If you are inside apps/web, pnpm dev is fine. If you are at taskflow root, filter to the package. Make the location
explicit rather than guessing.

Common error: port 3000 already used
Do not kill random processes. Identify which process owns the port, determine whether another dev server is already
running, and either reuse/stop it intentionally or choose a different port.

Production build is a different verification
Fast Refresh success does not prove the application is production-buildable. At the phase exit, run the web package
build from the workspace and fix type/lint/build failures before continuing.

Browser DevTools habits
•
Elements: inspect actual DOM and computed styles.
•
Console: client errors and logs.
•
Network: later inspect API requests, status codes and timing.
•
Application/Storage: later inspect browser-managed storage only when the feature actually uses it.
•
Accessibility tree where available: verify semantic output instead of visual appearance alone.
Debug by locating the failing boundary first

Symptom            locate   Which environment?      inspect    Collect evidence       hypothesis     Small fix

test

Repeat verification

Figure 1 - A disciplined loop is faster than rewriting code until the error disappears

Checkpoint
•
You can explain why NEXT_PUBLIC_ means browser-visible.
•
You know whether to inspect terminal or browser first for a given symptom.
•
You can diagnose Server/Client boundary errors without widening use client unnecessarily.
•
You use the production build as a phase gate.

lessons.body:
Phase 03

Exercises and Phase Exit
Practice Next.js independently, debug realistic failures, pass the
architecture oral exam, and verify readiness for NestJS.

Book 8 - Exercises

Course baseline: September 17, 2026 - Windows-first - Project-driven - Production-oriented

Exercises, Architecture Checks and Phase Exit
The phase is complete only when you can reproduce the ideas without following every line. These exercises move
from guided repetition toward independent engineering decisions.

Level 1 - Follow
•
Create the /projects and /settings routes from memory.
•
Add primary navigation in the root layout using Link.
•
Create one CSS Module and apply it to a project card.
•
Run dev, lint and build from the workspace root using a filter.

Level 2 - Modify
•
Add an /about route without changing the root layout API.
•
Add a descriptive empty state to /projects when the sample array is empty.
•
Improve visible keyboard focus for navigation links.
•
Add metadata appropriate for the application.

Level 3 - Implement
Create a small ProjectStatusFilter Client Component that switches between All, Active and Planning for static
sample projects. Keep the page as a Server Component if possible. Explain what data had to move into the client
island and why.

Level 4 - Engineer
Design a route structure for the future TaskFlow product without implementing backend data. Include dashboard,
projects, a future project-detail route, and settings. Decide where a dashboard layout would live, which sections
should share navigation, and where you would avoid route groups until the need is real.

Debugging scenarios
Scenario                                             Your diagnosis should start with

useState error in page.tsx                           Server/Client boundary; isolate interactive component

/projects is 404                                     Filesystem route structure and page.tsx location

CSS class undefined                                  CSS Module import/name mismatch

pnpm --filter web says no package matched            Check apps/web package name and workspace membership

Works in dev, fails build                            Read build/type error; do not assume Fast Refresh proved
correctness

Secret appears in browser bundle                     Treat as exposure; remove public prefix and redesign ownership

Architecture oral exam
•
Why can Next.js be called full-stack while this course still uses NestJS?
•
What is the difference between a route layout and a reusable UI component?
•
Why are Server Components the default?
•
What capabilities force a Client Component?
•
Why is use client at the root layout usually a poor first fix?
•
Why is NEXT_PUBLIC_ a security boundary?

•
Why do we build with static data before inventing an API that does not exist yet?

Expected answers - concise
•
Next.js vs NestJS: Next.js has server capabilities, but TaskFlow centralizes authoritative domain rules in NestJS
so there is one business API.
•
Layout vs component: a layout participates in the route tree and persists around descendant routes; a
component is reusable UI independent of route semantics.
•
Server default: non-interactive UI can render without shipping component JavaScript to the browser and can use
server capabilities.
•
Client requirement: browser event handlers, client hooks, browser APIs, or client-only libraries.
•
NEXT_PUBLIC_: it declares that a value may be included in browser-visible code; therefore secrets never belong
there.

Phase exit checklist
•
I can recreate apps/web inside a pnpm monorepo without nesting Git or lockfiles.
•
I understand App Router pages, layouts and route segments.
•
I can explain Server versus Client Components using capabilities and network boundary.
•
I can build internal navigation with Link.
•
I understand loading, error and not-found as distinct UI states.
•
I can style with global CSS and CSS Modules without mixing responsibilities.
•
I understand public versus server-only environment variables.
•
I can diagnose common Next.js errors using terminal and browser evidence.
•
I can produce a successful production build.

What changed in the architecture
BEFORE PHASE 03

taskflow repository
(no application runtime)

AFTER PHASE 03

Browser
^
|
Next.js App Router
|
apps/web
|
TaskFlow monorepo

No backend yet. No database yet.

Next phase preview
Phase 04 introduces a second independent runtime: NestJS with Fastify in apps/api. That phase will deliberately
keep the two applications separate. Only Phase 06 will connect them over HTTP, so the learner can understand
each side before crossing the network boundary.

Volume 02 - Frontend + Backend Foundations

Guided Build Lab — Phase 03: Next.js Fundamentals

Purpose
Build the Next.js application shell while understanding App Router routing, layouts, Server Components, Client Components, environment boundaries, and rendering behavior.

Deliverable
A navigable TaskFlow web shell with route groups/layouts, server-first composition, selective client interactivity, and verified environment handling.

Before you touch the code
Open the previous phase checkpoint, run the repository's verification commands, and make sure Git is clean. A guided lab is useful only when you know which change introduced a failure. Write down the current browser/API/database behavior you expect before modifying anything.

Architecture trace
Route request -> App Router match -> layout/page Server Component -> optional server fetch -> Client Component island -> browser interaction

Read this flow left to right, then right to left. For each arrow, say what data crosses the boundary, which side trusts the other, and what evidence would prove that this boundary works. This habit prevents framework APIs from becoming disconnected memorization.

Step 1 — Generate the web app in the monorepo and verify the development server from the correct workspace.
Do the smallest version of this step first. After the change, stop and verify it before continuing. Use terminal output, HTTP responses, browser DevTools, tests, or database inspection depending on the boundary. If the result differs from your prediction, do not add more code; explain the mismatch and fix the earliest failing assumption.

Step 2 — Create nested routes and a shared layout, then predict which layouts persist across navigation.
Do the smallest version of this step first. After the change, stop and verify it before continuing. Use terminal output, HTTP responses, browser DevTools, tests, or database inspection depending on the boundary. If the result differs from your prediction, do not add more code; explain the mismatch and fix the earliest failing assumption.

Step 3 — Build one component as a Server Component and identify exactly why it can remain server-only.
Do the smallest version of this step first. After the change, stop and verify it before continuing. Use terminal output, HTTP responses, browser DevTools, tests, or database inspection depending on the boundary. If the result differs from your prediction, do not add more code; explain the mismatch and fix the earliest failing assumption.

Step 4 — Add one Client Component for interaction and explain what 'use client' changes in the dependency graph.
Do the smallest version of this step first. After the change, stop and verify it before continuing. Use terminal output, HTTP responses, browser DevTools, tests, or database inspection depending on the boundary. If the result differs from your prediction, do not add more code; explain the mismatch and fix the earliest failing assumption.

Step 5 — Add server-only and public environment values and prove which can reach the browser bundle.
Do the smallest version of this step first. After the change, stop and verify it before continuing. Use terminal output, HTTP responses, browser DevTools, tests, or database inspection depending on the boundary. If the result differs from your prediction, do not add more code; explain the mismatch and fix the earliest failing assumption.

Step 6 — Use browser DevTools and terminal logs to distinguish server rendering from client execution.
Do the smallest version of this step first. After the change, stop and verify it before continuing. Use terminal output, HTTP responses, browser DevTools, tests, or database inspection depending on the boundary. If the result differs from your prediction, do not add more code; explain the mismatch and fix the earliest failing assumption.

Useful verification commands
pnpm --filter web dev
pnpm --filter web build

Do not run commands mechanically. Before each command, predict what successful output should prove. If it fails, capture the exact message and identify whether the failure is environment, dependency, compile-time, runtime, network, authorization, or persistence related.

Checkpoint
When the lab works, inspect git diff. Remove accidental debugging output and unrelated edits. Run type checking/tests/build commands relevant to this phase. Commit the checkpoint with a message that describes the capability added, not merely the files changed.

Explain-back
Without looking at the lesson, explain why each layer in the architecture trace exists, what this phase added to TaskFlow, and what would break if the new responsibility were moved to the wrong layer. If you cannot explain the boundary, repeat the trace before moving on.

lessons.summary:
Goal
Learn to diagnose this phase's failures systematically instead of reinstalling packages, changing random configuration, or copying a fix without understanding it.
lessons.body:
Debugging Workshop — Phase 03: Next.js Fundamentals

Goal
Learn to diagnose this phase's failures systematically instead of reinstalling packages, changing random configuration, or copying a fix without understanding it.

The debugging loop
1. Reproduce the failure with the smallest reliable action.
2. Capture the exact symptom: command, status code, stack trace, network request, database state, or UI state.
3. Locate the earliest boundary where actual behavior diverges from expected behavior.
4. Form one hypothesis.
5. Change one variable.
6. Re-run the same reproduction.
7. Keep the fix only if the evidence supports the hypothesis.

Boundary walk
Route request -> App Router match -> layout/page Server Component -> optional server fetch -> Client Component island -> browser interaction

Start at the visible symptom and walk backward. Do not debug the database when the browser never sent the request. Do not debug React state when the API is returning a deterministic 403. The boundary walk tells you which evidence to collect next.

Failure drill 1 — Adding 'use client' too high in the tree
Create or imagine this failure in a safe development environment. Write the expected symptom first. Then list the two or three observations that would distinguish this failure from neighboring causes. Repair it with the smallest change and verify the original reproduction no longer fails.

Failure drill 2 — Accessing browser APIs from Server Components

lessons.body:
Phase Synthesis & Independent Challenge — Next.js Fundamentals

Mission
Rebuild the capability of Phase 03 without following the exact code line-by-line. The goal is transfer: can you use the ideas when the variable names, UI, or route shape changes?

Required outcome
Build the Next.js application shell while understanding App Router routing, layouts, Server Components, Client Components, environment boundaries, and rendering behavior.

Required artifact
A navigable TaskFlow web shell with route groups/layouts, server-first composition, selective client interactivity, and verified environment handling.

Constraints
• Start from the previous phase checkpoint or a fresh branch.
• Use the course architecture boundaries, but do not copy the reference implementation until after your first attempt.
• Keep changes scoped to the capability.
• Preserve validation, authorization, error handling, and observability expectations already earned in earlier phases.
• Record any design decision where more than one implementation is reasonable.

Acceptance criteria
• Can choose server vs client intentionally.
• Can explain layout/page routing.
• Can identify where code executes.
• Can debug a hydration or environment-boundary mistake.

Independent build sequence
1. Generate the web app in the monorepo and verify the development server from the correct workspace.
2. Create nested routes and a shared layout, then predict which layouts persist across navigation.
3. Build one component as a Server Component and identify exactly why it can remain server-only.
4. Add one Client Component for interaction and explain what 'use client' changes in the dependency graph.
5. Add server-only and public environment values and prove which can reach the browser bundle.
6. Use browser DevTools and terminal logs to distinguish server rendering from client execution.

Self-review
Compare your implementation to the reference only after the acceptance criteria pass. Differences are not automatically mistakes. For each difference, ask: does it preserve the same contract, security boundary, correctness, maintainability, and operational behavior? Keep the alternative when you can justify it with evidence.

Stretch challenge
Change one assumption: more users, a second tenant, a slow network, an expired session, a concurrent mutation, a deployment restart, or a failed dependency. Predict whether your design still behaves correctly. If not, document the next architectural improvement rather than adding complexity blindly.

Phase exit
Run the relevant checks, inspect Git diff, and write a three-sentence summary: what the system can do now, which boundary owns the new responsibility, and which failure you now know how to diagnose. Only then mark the phase complete.

lessons.title: Mastery Capstone Lab

lessons.body:
Mastery Capstone Lab

This is the transfer exercise for Phase 03: Next.js Fundamentals. The detailed lessons are now closed-book reference material. Your task is to prove that the phase outcome can be reproduced from requirements, repository evidence, and debugging—not by copying a finished implementation.

Target artifact
A navigable TaskFlow web shell with route groups/layouts, server-first composition, selective client interactivity, and verified environment handling.

Acceptance criteria
- Write the behavior and constraints before implementation.
- Identify the owning layer and every boundary crossed.
- Implement the smallest complete vertical slice.
- Verify the happy path from outside the implementation.
- Demonstrate at least one expected failure path.
- Run the phase-relevant quality checks.
- Review the diff for accidental duplication, leaked responsibilities, missing validation/authorization, and hidden environment assumptions.

Evidence packet
Save the command/request used, expected result, actual result, one failure reproduction, the fix, and a short explanation of why the final responsibility belongs where it does. This packet is more valuable than a screenshot of a green page because it demonstrates repeatable engineering reasoning.

Stretch
Change one requirement after the first implementation. Measure which files must change. If a tiny domain change causes unrelated layers to move, use that evidence to discuss coupling before adding another abstraction.
